Anyone Can Build · Class 520 / 108
1958 · Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory · US Navy money1958年 · コーネル航空研究所 · 米海軍の資金

The perceptron: a machine that corrects itselfパーセプトロン：自分で自分を修正する機械

weights = all_zeros()                                    # one number for every pixel
for picture, answer in examples:                         # "this one is a 7"
    score = sum(pixel × weight, over every pixel)
    guess = "7" if score > 0 else "1"
    if guess != answer:                                  # only when it is wrong:
        if answer == "7": weights = weights + picture    # lean toward this 7
        else:             weights = weights - picture    # lean away from this 1
Frank Rosenblatt, 1958 · his learning rule, simplifiedフランク・ローゼンブラット、1958年 · 彼の学習ルールを簡単にしたもの

Bag of words · Naive Bayesバッグ・オブ・ワーズ · ナイーブベイズ

How counting picks a label数えることでラベルをどう選ぶか

# learn: count every word, in reviews already marked good or bad
for review, label in examples:                      # 700 good, 700 bad
    for word in review:
        count[label][word] += 1

# guess: how typical is each word of each side? multiply, then compare
for side in ["good", "bad"]:
    score[side] = multiply(share(word, side) for word in new_review)
guess = "good" if score["good"] > score["bad"] else "bad"
A statistical approach to evaluating labels.
Bag of words: which words appear, not how many, and not their order
What it needs: examples already labelled — 1,400 reviews someone had already marked good or bad · Pang, Lee & Vaithyanathan, 2002, simplified統計を使ってラベルを判定するやり方。
バッグ・オブ・ワーズ：どの語が出てくるか。何回出てくるかでも、順番でもない
必要なもの：すでにラベルのついた例 — 誰かがすでに良い・悪いの印をつけていたレビュー1,400件 · Pang, Lee & Vaithyanathan, 2002 を簡単にしたもの

The whole machine, in five lines機械の全体を5行で
text = "I'd like a cup of"
while True:
    chances = how_likely_is_each_next_word(last_word(text))   # 1948: only the word before
    word    = pick_one(chances)                               # chance decides
    text    = text + " " + word                               # and around again
    # it stops when it picks the special "stop" word — that is on the list too
The list is worked out the same way every time. The chance is in the pick.一覧は毎回同じやり方で計算される。偶然が入るのは、選ぶところだ。

Anyone Can Build · Class 580 / 108
Before 20172017年より前
Translating from memory.記憶から翻訳する。
It took in the whole English sentence, kept one summary of it, and wrote the French from that summary alone — never looking back at the English. A long sentence got the same small summary as a short one, so long sentences came out wrong. They called it the bottleneck.英語の文を丸ごと取り込み、その要約を一つだけ持ち、その要約だけからフランス語を書いた — 英語を振り返ることは一度もない。長い文も短い文と同じ小さな要約にされたので、長い文は間違って出てきた。これはボトルネックと呼ばれた。
Anyone Can Build · Class 581 / 108
Where attention came fromアテンションはどこから来たか
School translation exercises.学校での翻訳の練習。
Asked where he got the idea, its inventor described his gaze moving between the sentence he was reading and the one he was writing. He built it, it worked first time, and he called it RNN search. Somebody else gave it the better name.どこからその考えを得たのかと聞かれて、発明者は、読んでいる文と書いている文のあいだを行き来する自分の視線のことを語った。彼はそれをつくり、それは一度目でうまくいき、彼はそれをRNN searchと名づけた。もっといい名前をつけたのは別の人だった。
Anyone Can Build · Class 582 / 108
2017 · eight authors at Google · built to translate2017年 · Googleの8人の著者 · 翻訳のためにつくられた
“Attention Is All You Need”
The paper's title is its idea: delete the part that reads one word at a time, and keep only the looking-back. Now every word can be looked at at once, so it trains on far more text than anything before it. That is the T in GPT.論文のタイトルが、そのままアイデアだ：一語ずつ読む部分を消し、振り返る部分だけを残す。すると、すべての単語を一度に見られるので、それまでのどんなものよりもはるかに多くのテキストで学習できる。それがGPTのTだ。

You are the trainer · rank these, best to worstあなたが学習させる側 · いちばん良いものから悪いものへ、順位をつける

“Will my Japanese phone charger work in the US?”“日本のスマホの充電器は、アメリカでも使える？”

A
Almost certainly. Phone chargers are made for 100–240 volts — check the small print on yours. The plug is the same shape too, so you need no adapter.
B
Great question! Sadly, no — the US uses different electricity, so it won’t work there. But don’t worry, you can pick up a cheap one when you land! 😊
C
Electrical standards differ between countries, and it depends on your device. You may wish to check with the manufacturer before you travel.
Hands up for each. Which is best?
Anyone Can Build · Class 593 / 108
That is exactly how it was trainedまさにそうやって学習させられた

What could be wrong with eachそれぞれ、どこがまずいのか

A
Right, and it tells you how to check.
Japanese plugs fit American sockets, and most phone chargers take 100–240 volts. The one risk it leaves is an old charger made for 100 volts only — which is why it says check the small print.
B
Warm, confident — and wrong.
The charger almost certainly works. Believing this, you would buy a new one for nothing. It is the answer that feels nicest, which is the danger.
C
True, safe — and no answer at all.
Nothing in it is false, and nothing in it helps. It sounds careful because it never commits.
People ranked answers like these. The model was trained towards the ones people preferred.
Asked in French for a short story, the untrained model wrote more requests for stories. The trained one wrote the story. Opened to everyone as ChatGPT on 30 November 2022, it had over a million users within five days.フランス語で短い物語を頼まれると、学習させる前のモデルは物語を頼む文をさらに書いた。学習させたモデルは、物語を書いた。2022年11月30日にChatGPTとして誰でも使えるように公開されると、5日以内に利用者は100万人を超えた。

Before you reach for a language model言語モデルに手を伸ばす前に
Try the lowest tier that solves the problem.問題を解ける、いちばん下の階層を試す。
It costs less to run, answers faster, and is easier to check and to explain. Use a language model when nothing below it will do.動かすのが安く、答えが速く、確かめるのも説明するのも簡単。言語モデルは、それより下のどれでも足りないときに使う。

Before you hand anything over何かを任せる前に
  1. One exactly-right answer a program could work out? → ask for the programプログラムで求められる、ただ一つの正しい答えがあるか？ → プログラムを頼む
  2. Can I check it? → no check, don't hand it over確かめられるか？ → 確かめられないなら任せない
  3. What does being wrong cost? → expensive or permanent, you decide; it only advises間違いの代償は？ → 高くつく、取り返しがつかないなら、決めるのは自分。機械は助言するだけ
  4. Must I be able to defend it? → learning mode自分で説明できる必要があるか？ → 学習モード
